title: Yara and the Inheritance
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Brightwater — town founder and Freya's own grandfather — is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, night-shift dispatcher Freya Brightwater is the only person in Hollow Creek who refuses to accept the official story of clerical error. Following a decade-old dispatch log she was never supposed to read, she discovers that the sole witness to Aldous's real death, a taxi driver named Marisol Vane, was declared dead years ago to bury what she saw. As the anniversary dinner approaches and the family fortune hangs on proof that Aldous died intestate, Freya races to find Marisol alive before her uncle Silas can raise his glass over a forged will. She finds Marisol hiding in plain sight as the cemetery's groundskeeper, and together they expose Silas at the dinner itself — but justice comes outside the courtroom, when the town chooses memory over law.
about_author: Ulyana Zhou spent six years answering phones for a small-town cab company before turning those graveyard shifts into fiction. She writes mysteries about people whose jobs let them hear everything and be believed about nothing.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On her last shift before the anniversary week, Freya hears radio chatter about the exhumation ordered for the land dispute and drives to the cemetery at dawn, watching workers lift a lid on nothing but river stones. The beat: cold professional curiosity curdling into personal violation.

chapters.title: Dispatch Log 4471
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Digging through the taxi company's archived logs for the night Aldous supposedly died, she finds call 4471: a pickup from Brightwater House at 2:14 a.m., logged by a driver named Marisol Vane — a name with no payroll record and a death certificate dated three days later. Beat: the thrill of the hunt.

chapters.title: Uncle Silas Pours
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At a tense family lunch, Silas Brightwater smoothly explains away the empty coffin as Victorian paperwork errors and reminds everyone the estate hinges on the anniversary reading of the will. Freya notices he never once asks who found the grave empty. Beat: dread dressed as civility.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A records clerk, bribed with coffee and honesty, shows Freya that Marisol Vane's death certificate was filed by the same notary who witnessed Aldous's will. Two deaths, one pen. Beat: the case stops being strange and becomes deliberate.

chapters.title: Graveyard Shift
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Working her dispatch console overnight, Freya cross-references every cab call from Brightwater House across ten years and finds a pattern: calls that were logged but never billed, all signed off by Silas's late wife. Beat: loneliness of the night worker, sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Someone Follows the Cab
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. After Freya pulls the original paper log from storage, her apartment is searched and the log is gone — but the thief left a single river stone on her desk, straight from the coffin. Beat: fear arriving as a message: stop digging.

chapters.title: What the Groundskeeper Knows
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya interviews the cemetery's taciturn groundskeeper, Ruth Calloway, who mentions — unprompted — that Aldous Brightwater hated river stones. Freya files the slip away, saying nothing. Beat: the reader sees the answer before the detective does.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Silas announces the anniversary dinner will include the reading of a 'newly discovered' will leaving everything to him. Freya realizes the forgery needs the empty coffin to stay unexplained. Beat: the clock starts ticking toward the dinner.

chapters.title: Marisol's Route
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Reconstructing Marisol's last known route, Freya finds the driver's abandoned locker at the old depot: a journal describing the 2:14 a.m. pickup, Aldous alive and terrified, naming Silas. The final pages are torn out. Beat: vindication and fury in equal measure.

chapters.title: Dead Witness, Live Voice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Playing back decades of dispatch tapes hunting for Marisol's voice, Freya recognizes it — in a recent call reporting 'a disturbance at the cemetery.' Marisol made the call three weeks ago. She's alive, and she's close. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Silas Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Silas corners Freya, offering her the dispatcher job for life and her mother's medical debts paid, if she hands over anything she found in the depot. He never denies anything; he just prices it. Beat: temptation as threat.

chapters.title: Ruth's Hands
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya returns to the cemetery and catches Ruth tending a grave that isn't on any plot map — a marker with no name, fresh flowers, river stones arranged in a pattern. When Freya says 'call 4471,' Ruth drops the trowel. Beat: two watchers finally seeing each other.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. In the cemetery cottage, Ruth reveals herself as Marisol Vane: she faked her death after Silas threatened her, then buried the truth along with the man she couldn't save. She kept Aldous's ashes hidden under the nameless marker for ten years. Beat: grief finally given a witness.

chapters.title: Why the Coffin Was Empty
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol explains: Aldous died of a heart attack in her cab before he could destroy Silas's forged will; Silas staged the burial, kept the body's absence as leverage, and let the town mourn a box of stones. Beat: the mystery's spine laid bare.

chapters.title: Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The missing journal pages turn up slipped under Freya's door — someone else has been searching too, and they're ahead of her. She suspects Silas's lawyer, or Silas himself testing her. Beat: paranoia tightening like a ratchet.

chapters.title: Two Days to Dinner
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya and Marisol plan to expose Silas at the anniversary dinner, but Marisol insists on conditions: no police until after the toast, because the sheriff owes Silas. Freya must choose between procedure and justice. Beat: the theme made explicit — law versus right.

chapters.title: The Stone in the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya plants a decoy — a copy of the journal — and watches who comes for it. It's the notary's son, who confesses his father forged the will under duress and kept the original as insurance. Beat: the trap snapping shut on the wrong prey, then the right one.

chapters.title: Ashes and River Stones
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. On the eve of the dinner, Marisol digs up the urn she has guarded for a decade and asks Freya whether exposing the truth will give Aldous back his name or just take hers. Freya promises both can survive. Beat: quiet before the storm, love and doubt entwined.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Silas raises his glass to the founder's memory and presents the forged will. Freya stands, calls out dispatch log 4471, and produces the urn, the journal, and the notary's confession as the room goes silent. Beat: the climax — truth spoken aloud where lies expected applause.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The sheriff arrives loyal to Silas, but the town — dockworkers, clerks, cabbies who remember Marisol's face — physically bars the exit until the state investigator Freya secretly called takes custody of the evidence. Beat: the community itself becomes the verdict.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Weeks later, Aldous Brightwater is buried properly, his real will — recovered from the notary's safe — leaving the land to the town. Marisol Vane is legally resurrected, her death certificate voided. Beat: mourning finally allowed to do its work.

chapters.title: Night Shift, New Calls
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Back at the console, Freya takes a routine fare request and recognizes the address: Brightwater House, now a community trust. She signs off her shift, walks out into dawn, and lets herself cry for the first time since the exhumation. Beat: resolution — memory honored, inheritance shared, the dispatcher finally off duty.
